clue.text: Coming from haunts of coot and hern I was so quarrelsome

definitions.text: Coming from haunts of coot and hern I was so quarrelsome

parts.words: Coming from haunts of coot and hern I was so quarrelsome
parts.note: the speaker is Tennyson's brook, which comes from the haunts of coot and hern and in the poem chatters noisily down a valley, read here as squabbling

explanation.surface: A bird-watching walker grumbles that they came back from the marshes in a foul temper.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennyson's poem The Brook opens 'I come from haunts of coot and hern' and has the stream 'bicker down a valley'; the clue plays on bicker meaning both to flow noisily and to quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To bicker is to squabble pettily, and the brook in the poem is said to bicker as it runs.

clue.text: Caul ?

parts.note: a caul is the membrane that may cover a newborn's head, read as a hood worn in infancy

explanation.definitionFit: Babyhood is infancy, and the clue reads the word as a hood for a newborn, which is what a caul is.

clue.text: A sine qua non of a state

definitions.meaning: Latin for 'without which not', something absolutely required
the state something is in, its general health or order

explanation.definitionFit: A sine qua non is an essential prerequisite, a condition; a state of health or repair is also one's condition.

clue.text: It's in the index actually word for word

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the clue words that follow

explanation.surface: A remark that something appears in a book's index exactly as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact means precise and accurate, as a word-for-word copy is.

clue.text: Porphyro and Madeline were aye, ages long ago"

definitions.text: Porphyro and Madeline were aye, ages long ago"

parts.words: Porphyro and Madeline were aye, ages long ago"
parts.note: Keats ends The Eve of St Agnes with the two lovers fleeing together into the storm, 'aye, ages long ago'

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank question about the young lovers in Keats's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: In Keats's The Eve of St Agnes, Porphyro steals Madeline from her family's castle and they flee together.
explanation.definitionFit: Lovers who run away secretly to marry are eloping, as the couple in Keats's poem do.

clue.text: Transgress from start of a race to the finish

parts.note: a race begins with the call 'they're off', so the start is the off
the finish of something is its end

explanation.surface: An athlete breaks the rules all the way from the gun to the tape.
explanation.definitionFit: To offend is to break a rule or commit a wrong, the same as to transgress.

clue.text: It costs her something to go on her native river

definitions.text: It costs her something to go on her native river

indicators.note: to go on says the river follows the coin in the answer

parts.note: a franc was the coin a Frenchwoman paid things with
the Oise is a river of northern France

explanation.surface: A Frenchwoman pays to travel along a river in her homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a French girl's name, and its parts build it: the franc she spends, then a French river.
explanation.definitionFit: Françoise is a French woman's name, built from the French coin and the French river.

clue.text: Supremely erotic girl partial to the opera toreador

indicators.note: partial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sexy young woman is fond of the bullfighter in the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Partial to' reads as 'fond of', but it signals that only part of the following words is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of love and erotic poetry in Greek myth, a divine woman of passion.

clue.text: Hate to put up Edward about sundown

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up says the built letters are read from bottom to top
about says the short name goes around the other piece

parts.note: Ted is a short form of the name Edward
at sundown the sun sets, so sundown gives set

explanation.surface: Someone loathes having to give Edward a bed around nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: TED goes 'about' SET to make TSETED; 'put up' then reads it upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe or dislike intensely.

clue.text: Plead with one to depart

parts.note: to beg is to plead

explanation.surface: Someone pleads with another person to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Begone is an old command to go away, telling someone to leave.

clue.text: My! Sore at locating unlimited censorship!

parts.note: a ban is an act of censorship, forbidding something
galore means in abundance, without limit

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in irritation at being hit by boundless censorship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My! Sore' run together is MYSORE, the old Indian state whose capital was Bangalore, so the definition reads 'Mysore's location'. Clue order puts 'unlimited' first, but the answer takes BAN then GALORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bangalore was the capital city of the former Indian state of Mysore, so it is a place located in Mysore.

clue.text: A very large order

parts.note: vast means huge, very large

explanation.surface: Someone places an enormous order for goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' is a command here, not a purchase: the sailor's call to stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is a nautical command telling sailors to stop or hold.

clue.text: One among many to pull up

indicators.note: among says the letter for one goes inside the word for many

parts.note: a host is a great number, many
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A single person in a crowd is told to haul something up.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoist something is to raise or lift it, often with ropes.

clue.text: Result of ploughing school fields-—limited capital cover

explanation.surface: A farm report on the school's land turns to a short haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, crops grown on the playing fields of Eton, a famous English public school. 'Capital' is the head, so a 'limited capital cover' is a short head of hair: the Eton crop was a close bobbed women's haircut of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: Crops are what ploughed fields produce, and the Eton crop was a fashionable very short haircut for women.

clue.text: For second choice one has drinks from these sources

parts.note: the word or introduces the second choice in 'this or that'
the Roman numeral for one is I
gins are spirit drinks

explanation.surface: A drinker picks a second round of spirits and wonders where they came from.
explanation.definitionFit: Origins are the places or things from which something arises, its sources.

clue.text: One's in a 'sub-continent — no, a country of islands

indicators.note: in says the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: India is the subcontinent of southern Asia
One's is taken as the plural ones

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are in the Indian subcontinent, and is told it is an island nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as the plural, which sits inside INDIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a southeast Asian nation made up of thousands of islands.

clue.text: Varied music for solvers

parts.note: varied points to a famous set of orchestral variations by Elgar, and for solvers the title is also a word for a puzzle

explanation.surface: A puzzle-setter recommends a mixed playlist for crossword fans.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar's Enigma Variations is a set of variations, hence 'varied music'; the same word means a riddle, something for solvers.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a puzzle or mystery to be solved, and Elgar's Enigma Variations is music built from variations.

clue.text: One fate of treasures laid up on earth

definitions.text: One fate of treasures laid up on earth

parts.words: One fate of treasures laid up on earth
parts.note: Jesus warns in Matthew's gospel against storing treasure on earth, where moth and rust corrupt it

explanation.surface: A biblical warning about what happens to hoarded riches.
explanation.walkthrough: Matthew 6:19: 'Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt.'
explanation.definitionFit: Stored cloth and garments are spoilt by moth larvae eating holes in them, one fate the gospel names.

clue.text: No turning back — pedals round in frightful weather

indicators.note: round says the word for pedals goes around the other piece

parts.note: to cycle is to pedal a bicycle

indicators.note: turning back says the word no is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A cyclist refuses to turn round while pedalling through a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No turning back' reads as a refusal to retreat, but it is the instruction to reverse the word no before the pedalling word wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclones are violent rotating storms, about the worst weather there is.

clue.text: To love, Edward must get a " Yes " sometime

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
Ned is a short form of the name Edward
ay is an old or dialect word for yes

explanation.surface: A suitor named Edward hopes to win a yes to his proposal eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: One day means at some unspecified time in the future, as does sometime.

clue.text: It's called archaic

parts.note: the clue is a dictionary entry: an old poetic word meaning named or called

explanation.surface: A remark that something is labelled old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue can also be read as 'it is said to be archaic', and the word is itself archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Yclept is an old Middle English past participle meaning named, now used only for effect.

clue.text: How does a lotus-eater play the odd tin lyre ?

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of tin lyre are strange, put into a new order

explanation.surface: A question about how a dreamy idler would strum a peculiar tin instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The lotus-eaters of the Odyssey and Tennyson's poem lie in languid idleness, so they do everything without energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotus-eaters drift in idle torpor, so anything they do is done sluggishly, without effort.

clue.text: Starts further in, looks pushed in

definitions.meaning: a typist begins a line further from the margin

explanation.definitionFit: To indent a line is to set its start back from the margin; something dented has had hollows pressed into it.

clue.text: To get plastered fuddles Bude seaman

definitions.note: the definition is the verb to plaster, causing to get plastered, so it fits the answer as an infinitive

indicators.note: fuddles suggests the letters are muddled as if drunk

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor in the Cornish town of Bude drinks until he is plastered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastered' seems to mean drunk, alongside 'fuddles'; it is smeared. BUDE and AB are mixed together. Bude is a seaside town in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedaub is to smear something thickly, with paint or mud, so that it gets plastered.

clue.text: Like Neaera's hair (Milton)

parts.note: in Milton's Lycidas the poet imagines toying with the tangles of Neaera's hair

explanation.surface: A literary reference to a girl's hair as described by Milton.
explanation.walkthrough: Lycidas has 'Or with the tangles of Neaera's hair', so her hair is full of knots.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair full of tangles is knotted and twisted together, just as Milton pictures Neaera's.

clue.text: Devonian mouth waters

parts.note: a river in Devon whose name plus the word mouth gives a Devon seaside town

explanation.surface: Something mouth-watering from Devon.
explanation.walkthrough: Teignmouth is a town on the south Devon coast at the river's mouth; Devon is a county of southwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Teign is a river in Devon that flows out to sea at the town of Teignmouth.

clue.text: A catch in this ?

parts.note: catch sounds like a snag or trick, but here it is an angler's haul of fish, carried in a wicker basket

explanation.surface: A suspicious person asks whether there is a hidden snag.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket in which an angler keeps the fish caught.

clue.text: Ruddy infirm belief

indicators.note: in, split off the front of infirm, says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
ruddy means red in colour

explanation.surface: A red-faced invalid holds a faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Infirm' looks like a description of an invalid, but it must be split into 'in firm', the 'in' signalling the container and 'firm' giving the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of faith or set of beliefs.

clue.text: Otherwise a kind of stone

parts.note: lias is a blue-grey limestone found in southern England

explanation.surface: A geologist offers a different name for a type of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Alias means also known as, otherwise called, as in 'Smith alias Jones'.

clue.text: Naval lepidopterist ?

parts.note: a sailor who collects butterflies: the US naval lieutenant of Puccini's opera who wins and abandons Madama Butterfly

explanation.surface: A sailor with a hobby of collecting butterflies.
explanation.walkthrough: In Madama Butterfly the US Navy lieutenant marries Cio-Cio-San, called Butterfly, so he is a naval officer who caught a butterfly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieutenant Pinkerton is the naval officer in Puccini's opera who takes the heroine Butterfly as his bride.

clue.text: Prohibit a Burns hero getting the: bird

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit
Tam o' Shanter is the hero of a narrative poem by the Scottish poet Robert Burns

explanation.surface: A Burns character is banned and booed off stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the bird' looks like being jeered, but 'getting the' only links, and 'bird' is the definition: a small breed of chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of domestic fowl, a kind of bird.

clue.text: A way to distort sound that is amazing!

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: distort says the letters of sound are twisted out of shape into a new order

explanation.surface: A method of warping audio that leaves listeners stunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like noise, but it is anagram fodder for 'distort', which makes OUNDS from its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To astound is to amaze or astonish, so what astounds is amazing someone.
